from: chapitres 0 et 3 de la vidéo longue (accroche, crédits réglementaires)
hook: Tesla's first profit? *Paid by its rivals.*
paragraphs: In 2020, Tesla made its first full-year profit: {seven hundred and twenty-one million dollars.|$721 million.}
That same year, other carmakers paid it {one billion, five hundred and eighty million dollars.|$1.58 billion.}
Why? Governments limit how much a carmaker's cars can pollute, on average.
A company that sells lots of big gasoline vehicles may go over the limit. It can pay a penalty, or buy credits from a company that's under it.

And no one is more comfortably under the limit than a company that only sells electric cars. Those credits cost Tesla almost nothing to produce: "virtually pure profit", in the words of one industry newspaper.
In 2020, the credits were more than twice the size of Tesla's entire net profit. Full story on the channel.
